title: Portaless — own your site, answer the machines, extend it safely
description: A self-hosted publishing system with a cryptographic identity, a written policy for AI readers, and extensions that run in a sandbox.

props.title: Own your site. Answer the machines. Extend it safely.
props.subtitle: Portaless is a self-hosted publishing system: your content, your identity, your rules — with a written policy for the automated readers that now consume the public web.

props.text: The machines are answered, in writing

You decide, from the panel, who may read your site: the terms for search engines, AI assistants and model training. The site publishes them, in writing, and enforces the AI-input rule on signed agent requests; search and training are cooperative signals that a crawler must honor.

props.items:
shield :: Own the state :: Identity, content and policy live in a node you control — portable, verifiable, self-hosted.
bot :: Answer the machines :: One written policy decides who may read, and the site answers the same way to every reader.
package :: Extend it safely :: Third-party code runs in a sandbox, granted one capability at a time — never unrestricted access to the core.
server :: Self-host, no exposed database :: One command installs it; it runs without paid hosting and without a database on the internet.

props.text: Everything above is a JSON page of Atomic Elements rendered by Portaless's own engine — the same engine you edit from the panel. There is no hand-written HTML here: this home is the product's first real use case.

props.title: Honest answers
props.items:
Is it ready for production? :: It is in public Beta and honest about its limits: the plugin installer is behind a flag that is off by default until an external security review, and five of twelve plugin capabilities still answer an explicit 501.
Do I need a paid host? :: No. It runs on free static hosting (GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages) or self-hosted, and no database is exposed to the internet.
Does an AI reading my site have to identify itself? :: Only if you decide so. Reading public content requires no identity; when you ask who is reading, the reader proves control of a key it already holds — not another account with another company.
How is this different from a CMS? :: Extensions run in a sandbox and are granted capabilities one at a time; the core never certifies them, and your content is a projection of your own canonical state.

props.title: Ready when you are.
props.subtitle: Install it, publish, and decide who may read. With Docker and a browser, the first site takes about ten minutes.
